risks.title: Persistent Inflationary Pressures and Monetary Policy Uncertainty
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, with recent data showing a stalling of disinflationary progress. This creates uncertainty about the future path of monetary policy, with potential for further rate hikes.
risks.watch_for: August core PCE inflation data, Federal Reserve's September FOMC meeting statement and projections.

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Middle East Conflict Impact
risks.summary: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East is a significant source of uncertainty, leading to higher energy prices, renewed inflation, and potential disruptions to supply chains and global trade.
risks.watch_for: Escalation of hostilities in the Middle East, further commodity price volatility.

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and its Economic Implications
risks.summary: Robust investment in Artificial Intelligence is a key driver of US growth, particularly in business investment. However, it also presents risks, including potential disruptions to the labor market and inflationary pressures from AI-related capital expenditures.
risks.watch_for: Continued strong AI capital expenditures, labor market impacts of AI adoption, AI-driven price pressures.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)
J.P. Morgan Asset Management (Mid-Year Outlook 2026, June 17, 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (Got data? Monitoring the US economy, March 13, 2026)

risks.title: US Fiscal Deficits and Rising National Debt
risks.summary: The US faces large and growing federal budget deficits, projected to increase significantly as a percentage of GDP. This trend is leading to a substantial rise in national debt, posing long-term fiscal sustainability concerns.
risks.watch_for: CBO's updated projections on deficits and debt, legislative actions related to fiscal policy.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook, February 11, 2026)
Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook, February 1, 2026)
Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook, December 3, 2025)

risks.title: Labor Market Resilience Amidst Slowing Growth
risks.summary: While the US labor market has shown resilience with a stable unemployment rate, there are signs of slowing job growth. The interplay between AI, potential policy shifts, and overall economic momentum will be crucial.
risks.watch_for: Monthly nonfarm payroll reports, unemployment rate trends, wage growth data.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (Got data? Monitoring the US economy, March 13, 2026)

risks.title: Global Growth Slowdown and Divergent Economic Performance
risks.summary: Global growth is projected to slow in 2026, with emerging market and developing economies facing particular challenges. This divergence is influenced by factors like the Middle East conflict, trade policy, and varying levels of AI adoption.
risks.watch_for: IMF and World Bank global growth forecasts, regional economic performance data.

risks.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Tariffs
risks.summary: Ongoing trade policy uncertainty and the potential for increased tariffs continue to pose risks to the global economy, impacting trade flows, inflation, and business investment.
risks.watch_for: Announcements of new tariffs or trade agreements, changes in trade dispute resolutions.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)
Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook, February 1, 2026)

risks.title: Potential for Market Volatility and Asset Valuations
risks.summary: Elevated geopolitical uncertainty, shifting monetary policy expectations, and the rapid rise of AI-related assets contribute to potential market volatility. Concerns exist about the valuations of some technology-driven assets.
risks.watch_for: S&P 500 performance, corporate earnings reports, shifts in market sentiment.
sources: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (Mid-Year Outlook 2026, June 17, 2026)

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus among institutions regarding the persistent nature of inflation and the significant impact of geopolitical tensions, particularly the conflict in the Middle East, on global economic stability and energy prices. While AI investment is seen as a key growth driver, its inflationary and labor market implications are viewed with caution. Disagreements or varying emphasis appear in the outlook for monetary policy, with some anticipating further tightening while others expect a hold, and in the precise trajectory of global growth, with some forecasts being more optimistic than others.
themes: Inflationary persistence and monetary policy response
Geopolitical risks and their economic spillovers
The transformative and disruptive impact of Artificial Intelligence
Fiscal sustainability and rising public debt
Resilience and evolution of labor markets
